messages:
carmen: paging — ECC error-rate burst observed in cluster-gpu-usw2 around 02:10 UTC. multiple nodes reported transient ECC counts then entered kernel-drain. alert noise + actual node drains. opening thread to coordinate mitigation and tuning. attaching quick links: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/gpu-health/cluster-usw2 and logs: https://logs.redwood.com/query?range=1h

sre-bot: Incident INC-4521 created: ECC_BURST_NODE_DRAIN | cluster-gpu-usw2 | severity: page. On-call: carmen. Paging list notified.

matt: thanks carmen. do we have any customer-facing impact? reduced throughput or 5xx spikes?

carmen: short answer: yes but limited. we saw a few model alloc failures and OOM-like allocation errors when a node drained mid-request. roughly ~0.5% of requests in the region got transient 500s, mainly long-context batches from a single mid-market customer running chunked generation. tail latency spiked for ~6 minutes while autoscale redistributed pods. no data exfiltration or S3 errors.

izzy: can you paste the key metrics? ECC rate, GPU temp, memory used, drain events timeline? also curious if this correlates with scheduled maintenance or infra noise.

carmen: quick paste from grafana:
- ECC error count (node-23, node-31): spike at 02:10 -> 02:13, ~120 errors over 3m window
- GPU temp: node-23 max 78C (normal for load)
- VRAM used: 92% on node-31 for long-context jobs
- Kernel-drain events: node-23 auto-drain triggered at 02:12, node-31 drained 02:14
- Eviction count: 2

leo: so two things: 1) ECC bursts that are short but trigger auto-drain + alerts = huge noise. 2) high VRAM on some nodes exacerbates impact when a drain happens. we should both mitigate for customers and reduce noisy pages.

carmen: mitigation steps taken (done):
- scaled up dedicated fallback pool (fallback-pool-02) to absorb allocations for ~10m
- temporarily disabled auto-drain threshold for ECC transient spikes (we lowered sensitivity back after stabilization) — we set the controller to require sustained ECC errors over 3m instead of instantaneous threshold (manual patch applied)
- cordoned node-23 and node-31, migrated critical pods to fallback pool
- opened contact to vendor support: nvidia-bot notified for telemetry dump

ops-bot: executed: kubectl drain node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30 

nvidia-bot: Received telemetry dump request. Engaging support. ETA initial analysis 2h. Provide dmesg + nvidia-smi logs for node-23 and node-31.

matt: thanks — for the alert tuning side, I'd prefer we don't completely disable alerts. we should: 1) require sustained error-rate, 2) aggregate per-pod or per-node to avoid duplicate pages, 3) add a suppression window when two nodes drain at once. can we prototype a Prometheus rule?

carmen: yes, suggested rule (prototype):
```yaml
- alert: ECCTransientBurst
  expr: increase(nvidia_gpu_ecc_uncorrectable_errors_total[3m]) > 50
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "ECC transient burst on {{ $labels.instance }}"
    runbook: "https://redwood.dev/runbooks/ecc-burst"
```
notes: increased window to 3m and for:5m to avoid 1-off blips causing pages. also add `sum by (node)` to roll up multiple GPU cards on a node.

izzy: add `sum by (node) (increase(...[3m]))` and set > 100 for node-level. then have separate alert for per-gpu that escalates only if sustained > 200 over 5m. also add label `auto_drain_eligible: true/false` to tie into the drain controller so we don't auto-drain on low-severity warnings.

leo: plus VRAM saturation alert: it's the secondary cause. propose new panel + alert:
```yaml
- alert: HighGPUVramUtilization
  expr: avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_memory_used_bytes / nvidia_gpu_memory_total_bytes[2m]) > 0.9
  for: 4m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU VRAM > 90% on {{ $labels.node }}"
```
this will catch nodes that are brittle during drains.

matt: agree. additional noise reduction: use alert grouping in PagerDuty to collapse multiple ECC alerts into one incident per-node with a dedupe window of 10m. also create a Grafana alert with `no_data` policy set to warn instead of page when panels briefly lose scrape.

carmen: i'll open two follow-up tickets: TKT-2345 (alert-rule change + controller tie-in) and TKT-2346 (dashboard + runbook updates). Also I'll attach the CLI changes we used to patch the drain controller.

izzy: i'll take handoff for the post-incident review and confirm runbook updates. on-call shift starts in 20m, so i'll be primary for follow-ups. can you add me to INC-4521 and assign TKT-2345->me?

carmen: done. INC-4521 updated with Izzy as incident lead and notes on mitigation. TKT-2345 assigned to izzy, owner set.

sre-bot: Handoff recorded: oncall -> izzy. Escalation window set for 2h for vendor analysis.

izzy: immediate next steps for me: 1) validate Prom rule in staging and roll to prod behind feature flag, 2) onboard a Grafana panel with node-level ECC rollup and VRAM summary, 3) update runbook section on when to auto-drain vs cordon. i'll ping when prod rule is live.

carmen: thanks team. final notes: customers notified (on a case-by-case basis) for those who saw 500s; CS queued email templates. we'll include mitigations in the postmortem. tagging: @oncall rotation for visibility. :white_check_mark:
